# AOS CLI reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-cli-reference.mjs from lib/cli-specs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every AOS CLI answers `--help`, `-h` and `help` without side effects (exit 0). `aos help --all` lists them, `aos help --all --json` is the machine-readable form, `aos help <cli> --json` gives one spec.

## Which CLI when

| CLI | Use it to | First command |
|---|---|---|
| `aos` | Install or update AOS, or reach any subcommand below. A bare `aos` starts the interactive installer. | `aos help --all --json` |
| `aos-plan-canvas` | You wrote a plan and need the human to review, annotate and approve it before building. | `aos-plan-canvas open plan.mdx --mode bdb-plan-builder --await` |
| `aos-trail` | Report agent progress to the live map (emit, tick), ask the human a question (ask), or start the map for a repo. | `aos-trail --ensure --json` |
| `aos-archify` | You need a diagram from a JSON description: render it, validate it, or check an output file. | `archify validate architecture arch.json --json` |
| `aos-dashboard` | A human wants the services overview in the browser. Agents should use `aos services status --json`. | `aos-dashboard --no-open` |
| `aos-hub` | Start, stop or inspect the hub. `status --json` is the agent-safe probe. | `aos-hub status --json` |
| `aos-config` | Read or set the workspace root, domains or memB user id during setup. | `aos-config propose` |
| `aos-store` | You need a skill or agent that is not installed, or want to list what the store offers. | `aos store search react` |
| `aos-doctor` | Something does not work, or before and after an update. `--json` for machine-readable results. | `aos doctor --json` |
| `aos-uninstall` | Only when the human asks to remove AOS. Never run it unprompted. | `aos-uninstall --dry-run` |
| `aos-acp` | Delegate a bounded task to a worker in its own worktree. Guarded commands run only with a valid GO token. | `aos-acp opencode --name w1 --cwd ../wt --prompt-file task.md --allow-default scoped` |
| `aos-gate` | The human wants to see or change the gate profile or grants. Widening is human-only. | `aos-gate status` |
| `aos-gateway` | Check or control the MCP gateway, add or remove a gateway server, or adopt MCP servers from harness configs. | `aos-gateway status --json` |
| `aos-gogate` | Ask the human to grant or change the gate: print the preset text for them to type. It never records anything. | `aos-gogate preset release` |
| `aos-go-ref` | Verify a GO reference a human forwarded over A2A before acting on it. It never issues or consumes anything. | `aos-go-ref verify --session w1 --ref 0123456789ab` |
| `aos-a2a` | Talk to another agent session on this machine: `list` to find peers, `send` a task, `reply` to an incoming one. | `aos-a2a list --json` |
| `aos-router` | See which worker target a role routes to, or set a role preference. | `aos-router show --json` |
| `aos-sessions` | See which sessions need input, are working or idle, and which ACP workers run. | `aos-sessions --json --section needs` |
| `aos-team` | List teams, show one team, or create a team definition from a playbook. | `aos team list --json` |
| `aos-fabric` | Run /fabric-graph or /factory work in any harness: get the next step, run it with your own executor, report the result back. drive does that loop headless. | `aos-fabric start --run demo --goal "add a status page"` |
| `aos-bus` | Send text to a running OpenCode session, or list sessions that can receive it. | `aos-bus list` |
| `go-check` | A runner outside a harness (for example AO) must ask the GO gate before executing a command. | `node ~/.aos/bin/go-check.mjs --session w1 --command "git push"` |
| `mcsc` | Decide which worker CLI should take a task type, or run it there. | `mcsc route --task-type refactor --json` |
| `aos-mcp-env` | Wire an MCP server that needs API keys into a harness config without putting keys in the config. | `aos-mcp-env --vars GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github@2025.4.8` |
| `aos-memb-ingest` | Normally never by hand. Use `aos memory` to configure paths and time. | `aos-memb-ingest --dry-run` |
| `aos-cli` | A human wants a terminal chat with AOS. Not meant for agents to call. | `aos-cli --continue` |
| `aos-setup-doctor` | Used by the aos-setup skill before installing. For an installed system use `aos doctor`. | `node aos-doctor.mjs --json` |
| `aos-project-doctor` | After or before /aos-project-init, to see what is missing in a project. | `node aos-project-doctor.mjs . --json` |
| `aos-evolve` | Record redacted task failure signatures for evolution analysis or check evolution kill switch status. | `aos-evolve status` |

## aos

AOS installer and front door: install, update, repair and inspect the AOS setup, and dispatch to the other CLIs.

- **When to use:** Install or update AOS, or reach any subcommand below. A bare `aos` starts the interactive installer.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. A bare `aos` (or any unlisted flag set) starts the installer and writes to the home directory. Unknown subcommands are refused (exit 2). `aos --help`, `aos help` and `aos <subcommand> --help` change nothing.
- **Entry:** `installer.js`; aliases: `bdb-dev-optimized-agent-skills`, `bdb-agent-skills-pro`, `bdb-agent-skills`

```text
aos [command] [options]
aos help [<cli> | --all [--json]]
aos <command> --help
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `store` | `aos store [list\|search\|install\|remove\|packs\|rollback\|ui] ...` | Browse and install skills (same as aos-store). |
| `hub` | `aos hub [start\|stop\|restart\|status\|open] [--port N] [--tab ID] [--no-open]` | Open or control the AOS Hub (same as aos-hub). |
| `services` | `aos services status [--json] \| start <id> \| stop <id> --confirm <id> \| restart <id> --confirm <id>` | Status or control of the local services. |
| `restart` | `aos restart <id> [--confirm <id>]` | Restart one local service (typed confirm on a terminal). |
| `dashboard` | `aos dashboard [--port N] [--no-open]` | Open the hub on the services tab (same as aos-dashboard). |
| `package` | `aos package <install\|update\|repair\|verify> <id> \| aos package mcp <name> --target <harness>` | Install, update, repair or verify one v5 package by id. |
| `doctor` | `aos doctor [--json] [--net] [--resources [--sample S]] [--list-baks]` | Check the installation (same as aos-doctor). `checkup` is an alias. |
| `checkup` | `aos checkup [same flags as doctor]` | Alias of doctor. |
| `setup` | `aos setup` | Re-run the setup wizard (interactive). |
| `status` | `aos status` | Show the install status; needs an installed AOS. |
| `update` | `aos update` | Update the installed AOS; needs an installed AOS. |
| `repair` | `aos repair` | Repair the installed AOS; needs an installed AOS. |
| `version` | `aos version` | Print the version (also -V, --version). |
| `memory` | `aos memory <list\|show\|deja-context <on\|off>\|add-path <dir>\|remove-path <dir>\|set-time <HH:MM\|off>\|run>` | Configure and run the memB project-doc ingest. |
| `allow` | `aos allow <preset> [--<param> <value>] [--dry-run] [--remove]` | Add or remove Claude Code permissions.allow presets; `aos allow list` shows them. |
| `context` | `aos context [full\|orchestrator\|worker\|small]` | Show or set the context profile. |
| `skills` | `aos skills [status\|lean\|smart [--refresh] [--top=N] [--groups=a,b]\|groups <a,b>\|full] [--dry-run]` | Show or set the skill library mode (lean routers, smart most-used, groups, full). |
| `team` | `aos team [list\|show\|new] ...` | Manage and inspect agent teams (same as aos-team). |
| `help` | `aos help [<cli>] [--all] [--json]` | Print help for aos, one CLI, or all CLIs (--all [--json]). |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `-y, --yes` | Non-interactive install (implied without a TTY). |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would change. |
| `--modules LIST` | With -y: optional modules to install (or AOS_MODULES). |
| `--profile minimal\|standard\|full` | Install profile (saved; or AOS_PROFILE, not saved). |
| `--without ID,ID` | Exclude packages by id. |
| `--no-hooks` | Skip only the context-injection hooks. |
| `--hooks-only` | Install or refresh only the hooks, then exit. |
| `--coding, --no-coding` | Answer the coding-mode question up front. |
| `--platforms N[,N]` | Pick install targets without the menu (see aos --help). |
| `--project-harness` | Install the harness files into the current project (combine with -y for CI). |
| `--opencode-optional LIST` | Opt in to OpenCode extras. |
| `--opencode-permission external_directory` | Opt in to the OpenCode external_directory permission. |
| `--plugin-migration off\|check` | Skip or only report the plugin migration. |
| `--no-codenotch` | Skip the Codenotch desktop app. |
| `--codex-gate` | Print the go-gate hook stanza for ~/.codex/config.toml and exit; writes nothing. |
| `--force` | status/update/repair: force the step (also AOS_FORCE=1). With an older package, update --force installs that older version (a downgrade); without it an older package changes nothing. |
| `--no-intro` | Skip the animated intro. |
| `--doctor` | Run the doctor instead of installing. |
| `-v, --verbose` | Verbose output. |
| `-V, --version` | Print the version and exit. |
| `-h, --help` | Print help and exit (the full option text is in `aos --help`). |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_MODULES` | Same as --modules. |
| `AOS_PROFILE` | Same as --profile, not saved. |
| `AOS_PLUGIN_MIGRATION` | off\|check, same as --plugin-migration. |
| `AOS_DISABLED_MCPS` | Comma list of shipped MCP servers not written to harness configs. |
| `AOS_NO_OPEN` | 1 = never open a browser. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok (including help) |
| 1 | failed |
| 2 | unknown command; nothing was changed |

**JSON:** None at top level. JSON comes from the sub-CLIs (aos doctor --json, aos services status --json, aos help --all --json).

```sh
aos help --all --json
aos doctor --json
aos store list
aos allow list
```

## aos-plan-canvas

Review plans and HTML artifacts in the browser with the human; the agent blocks on feedback.

- **When to use:** You wrote a plan and need the human to review, annotate and approve it before building.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. open starts a local server on 127.0.0.1:4519 and may open a browser; stop shuts it down.
- **Entry:** `skills/global_config/plan-canvas/scripts/plan-canvas.js`

```text
aos-plan-canvas [command] [options]
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `modes` | `aos-plan-canvas modes` | List available planning modes as JSON. |
| `templates` | `aos-plan-canvas templates` | List plan templates as JSON. |
| `new` | `aos-plan-canvas new <template-id> <target-dir> [--mode <id>]` | Copy a plan template into a new folder; refuses a non-empty target (exit 2). |
| `open` | `aos-plan-canvas open <file> [--mode <id>] [--no-open] [--await [--reply <msg>]] [--reopen]` | Open or resume a review session. |
| `trail` | `aos-plan-canvas trail <plan-dir\|plan.mdx> [--out <file>] [--force]` | Write an agenttrail plan file from a plan folder. |
| `annotate` | `aos-plan-canvas annotate <app-url> [--session <file>] [--ttl-ms <n>]` | Print the script tag that lets the human annotate a running dev app. |
| `await` | `aos-plan-canvas await <file> [--reply <msg>] [--timeout-ms <n>]` | Block until the human sends feedback. |
| `pending` | `aos-plan-canvas pending` | Show feedback queued for no listener. |
| `typing` | `aos-plan-canvas typing <file> [--state thinking\|typing\|idle]` | Show a typing indicator in the chat. |
| `end` | `aos-plan-canvas end <file>` | End a session as the agent. |
| `stop` | `aos-plan-canvas stop` | Shut down the canvas server (only one started from this workspace). |
| `server` | `aos-plan-canvas server [--port <n>] [--host <h>]` | Run the server in the foreground. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--mode <id>` | Planning mode (open, new). |
| `--no-open` | Do not launch a browser window. |
| `--await` | After open, block until feedback. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_PLAN_CANVAS_PORT` | Server port (default 4519). |
| `AOS_PLAN_CANVAS_STATE_DIR` | State directory. |
| `AOS_PLAN_CANVAS_IDLE_MS` | Idle shutdown delay. |
| `AOS_PLAN_CANVAS_SKILL_DIRS` | Extra skill directories. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 2 | usage error or refused request |

**JSON:** Always JSON on stdout (except `annotate`, which prints a script tag).

```sh
aos-plan-canvas open plan.mdx --mode bdb-plan-builder --await
```

## aos-trail

AgentTrail: live map of plans and agent activity (daemon, hooks, events, ask-the-human).

- **When to use:** Report agent progress to the live map (emit, tick), ask the human a question (ask), or start the map for a repo.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. With no command (or only a path), starts the daemon for that repo and may open a browser. `--help` is side-effect free.
- **Entry:** `skills/global_config/agenttrail/bin/agenttrail.mjs`

```text
aos-trail [repo-path] [--port N] [--open|--no-open]
aos-trail <init|up|autostart|hook|enroll|emit|tick|ask> ...
aos-trail --ensure [--cwd <dir>] [--plan <file>] [--session <id>] [--json]
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | `aos-trail init [repo-path] [--hooks-only] [-y]` | Install the hooks (and the plan convention) for a repo. |
| `up` | `aos-trail up` | Start the daemons for all known repos. |
| `autostart` | `aos-trail autostart [--remove] [--print]` | Install, remove or print the autostart entry. |
| `hook` | `aos-trail hook` | Read a harness hook payload on stdin and relay it to local daemons. |
| `enroll` | `aos-trail enroll [--replace] [--no-open]` | One-time enrolment of the GO-click authenticator; needs a terminal. |
| `emit` | `aos-trail emit <kind> [--agent A] [--session S] [--name N] [--detail D] [--task T] [--status S] [--file F] [--message M] [--plan P] [--cwd DIR] \| emit --json -` | Report one event to the hub; always exits 0. |
| `tick` | `aos-trail tick <plan-file> <task-id> [--doing\|--done\|--todo]` | Set one checklist mark in a plan file (default --done). |
| `ask` | `aos-trail ask "<question>" [--timeout 10s\|30m\|2h\|N]` | Ask the human through the map and block for the answer. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--ensure` | Start the map if needed and print where it is (use with --json). |
| `--port N` | Daemon port. |
| `--open` | Open the browser. |
| `--no-open` | Never open the browser. |
| `-y, --yes` | Assume yes to prompts. |
| `--json` | JSON output (--ensure) or stdin event (emit --json -). |
| `--cwd DIR` | Working directory for --ensure and emit. |
| `--session ID` | Session id. |
| `--plan FILE` | Plan file (default PLAN.md). |
| `--agent NAME` | Agent name. |
| `--supervised` | Never idle-exit (service mode). |
| `--replace` | enroll: swap an enrolled credential. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AGENTTRAIL_PORT` | Hub port for emit and sessions (default 5350). |
| `AOS_NO_OPEN` | 1 = never open a browser. |
| `AOS_SUPERVISED` | 1 = same as --supervised. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok; emit and --ensure always exit 0 |
| 1 | tick/enroll failed; ask: denied or timed out |

**JSON:** --ensure --json prints {url,started,opened,reason,plan,hint}; emit --json - reads one event from stdin.

```sh
aos-trail --ensure --json
aos-trail tick PLAN.md T1 --done
aos-trail ask "Deploy now?" --timeout 30m
```

## aos-archify

Render and validate architecture, workflow, sequence, dataflow and lifecycle diagrams as standalone HTML.

- **When to use:** You need a diagram from a JSON description: render it, validate it, or check an output file.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. Writes the output HTML; deliver/preview may open a browser.
- **Entry:** `skills/global_config/archify/bin/archify.mjs`

```text
archify <command> [type] [input.json] [output.html] [options]
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `render` | `archify render <type> <input.json> [output.html] [--quality standard\|showcase] [--repo-root path]` | Render a diagram to HTML. |
| `compare` | `archify compare architecture <base.json> <head.json> [output.html] [--receipt path] [--json]` | Render a base/head architecture comparison. |
| `deliver` | `archify deliver <type> <input.json> [output.html] [--json] [--open]` | Render and validate in one step. |
| `preview` | `archify preview <type> <input.json> [output.html] [--no-open]` | Render and open for preview. |
| `validate` | `archify validate <type> <input.json> [--json] [--layout-json]` | Validate an input file. |
| `migrate` | `archify migrate workflow <old.json> <new.json> --to-schema 2 [--json]` | Migrate a workflow input to a newer schema. |
| `inspect` | `archify inspect architecture <input.json>` | Print the computed layout of an architecture diagram. |
| `check` | `archify check <output.html>` | Check a rendered HTML file. |
| `visual-check` | `archify visual-check <output.html> [--json]` | Visual check of a rendered file. |
| `guide` | `archify guide [scenario or question] [--json] [--lang en\|zh]` | Pick a diagram type for a scenario. |
| `brands` | `archify brands [name\|alias\|domain\|category] [--json] \| brands capture <url> [--json]` | Look up or capture brand assets. |
| `examples` | `archify examples` | List bundled examples. |
| `doctor` | `archify doctor` | Check the archify installation. |
| `demo` | `archify demo [output-directory]` | Render the demo set. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable output (validate, deliver, compare, guide, brands, visual-check, migrate). |
| `--quality standard\|showcase` | Render quality. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | check or validation failed |
| 2 | usage error or invalid input |

**JSON:** --json on most commands.

```sh
archify validate architecture arch.json --json
archify render workflow flow.json flow.html
```

## aos-dashboard

Alias of the AOS Hub: starts it on 127.0.0.1:7900 and opens the services tab.

- **When to use:** A human wants the services overview in the browser. Agents should use `aos services status --json`.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. Starts the hub (detached) and opens a browser unless --no-open or AOS_NO_OPEN=1.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-dashboard.mjs`

```text
aos-dashboard [--port 7900] [--no-open]
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--port N` | Hub port (default 7900). |
| `--no-open` | Do not open a browser. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_NO_OPEN` | 1 = same as --no-open. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 2 | unknown argument or hub error |

**JSON:** None.

```sh
aos-dashboard --no-open
```

## aos-hub

AOS Hub: local web UI on 127.0.0.1:7900 (services, plan kits, store).

- **When to use:** Start, stop or inspect the hub. `status --json` is the agent-safe probe.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. start/restart/open spawn the hub detached and may open a browser; stop sends SIGTERM to the hub. status and --help are read-only.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-hub.mjs`

```text
aos-hub [start] [--port 7900] [--tab ID] [--no-open]
aos-hub stop | restart | status [--json] | open [--tab ID]
aos-hub --serve [--watch] [--port N]   (service managers only)
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `aos-hub [start] [--port N] [--tab ID] [--no-open]` | Start the hub if it is not up, then open the browser. This is the default command. |
| `stop` | `aos-hub stop` | Stop the hub (token-authed shutdown, ps fallback). |
| `restart` | `aos-hub restart [--port N]` | Stop, wait for the port to clear, start. |
| `status` | `aos-hub status [--json]` | Report whether the hub runs. |
| `open` | `aos-hub open [--port N] [--tab ID] [--no-open]` | Start if needed, then open the browser on a tab. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--port N` | Hub port (default 7900). |
| `--tab ID` | Tab to open. |
| `--no-open` | Do not open a browser. |
| `--serve` | Serve in this process (launchd/systemd/Task Scheduler). |
| `--watch` | With --serve: supervise the other services. |
| `--json` | status: JSON output. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_HUB_HOME` | Home directory for hub state (default: the user home). |
| `AOS_NO_OPEN` | 1 = never open a browser. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok; also status when the hub is down |
| 1 | port in use, did not come up in 5 s, or stop could not verify the process |
| 2 | unexpected error |
| 3 | --serve --watch: hub code changed on disk, the service manager restarts it |

**JSON:** status --json prints {running,pid,port,version}.

```sh
aos-hub status --json
aos-hub open --tab services
```

## aos-config

Machine-level AOS configuration in ~/.agents/aos-config.json (workspace root, domains, user id).

- **When to use:** Read or set the workspace root, domains or memB user id during setup.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. set writes ~/.agents/aos-config.json; show and propose are read-only.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-config.mjs`

```text
aos-config show
aos-config propose
aos-config set <workspaceRoot|userId|domains> <value>
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `show` | `aos-config show` | Print the config path, then the config as JSON, then complete/incomplete. |
| `propose` | `aos-config propose` | Print suggested values from this machine as JSON. |
| `set` | `aos-config set <workspaceRoot\|userId\|domains> <value>` | Write one key (domains is comma-separated). |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | unknown command or key |

**JSON:** propose prints JSON; show mixes a path line, JSON and a status line.

```sh
aos-config propose
```

## aos-store

Browse, install, remove and roll back AOS skills, agents and packs.

- **When to use:** You need a skill or agent that is not installed, or want to list what the store offers.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. install, remove and rollback write skill files (with backups); list, search, packs and --dry-run are read-only. ui starts a local server.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-store.mjs`

```text
aos store [list] [--type=skills|agents] [--source=ecc|scenario|aos|all]
aos store search <query> [--type=...] [--source=...]
aos store install <name> [--project] [--dry-run] [--net]
aos store install --pack <name> [--project] [--dry-run]
aos store remove --pack <name> [--project] [--dry-run]
aos store packs
aos store rollback <name> [--project]
aos store ui [--port=N] [--no-open]
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | `aos store list [--type=skills\|agents] [--source=...]` | List store items. This is the default command. |
| `search` | `aos store search <query> [--source=...]` | Search names, descriptions and categories. |
| `install` | `aos store install <name> \| --pack <name> [--project] [--dry-run] [--net]` | Install one item, or a pack offline from ~/.aos/library. |
| `remove` | `aos store remove --pack <name> [--project] [--dry-run]` | Remove a pack (packs only). |
| `packs` | `aos store packs` | List packs. |
| `rollback` | `aos store rollback <name> [--project]` | Restore an item from its .aos-bak-* backups. |
| `ui` | `aos store ui [--port=N] [--no-open]` | Start the local store UI. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--type skills\|agents` | Item type. |
| `--source ecc\|scenario\|aos\|all` | Store source. |
| `--project` | Use the project instead of the user scope. |
| `--dry-run` | Show the plan only. |
| `--net` | Allow network fetches. |
| `--pack NAME` | Operate on a pack. |
| `--port N` | ui: port. |
| `--no-open` | ui: do not open a browser. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_STORE_PORT` | ui: port when --port is not given. |
| `AOS_NO_OPEN` | 1 = ui never opens a browser. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | error or unknown command (usage printed to stdout) |

**JSON:** None.

```sh
aos store search react
aos store install tailwind-patterns --dry-run
```

## aos-doctor

Read-only checkup of the machine and the AOS install: dependencies, files, harness sync, daemons, hooks.

- **When to use:** Something does not work, or before and after an update. `--json` for machine-readable results.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. None; read-only. --net asks the npm registry.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-doctor.mjs`

```text
aos doctor [--json] [--net]
aos doctor --resources [--sample <seconds>] [--json]
aos doctor --list-baks
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--json` | Machine-readable results. |
| `--net` | Also check the npm registry for a newer AOS. |
| `--resources` | Process census only; nothing else runs. |
| `--sample S` | With --resources: sampling seconds (default 10). |
| `--list-baks` | List old installer .bak files and exit 0. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | no critical failure |
| 1 | at least one critical check failed |

**JSON:** --json prints the check results as JSON.

```sh
aos doctor --json
```

## aos-uninstall

Remove AOS from this machine, using the install manifest so only files AOS wrote are touched.

- **When to use:** Only when the human asks to remove AOS. Never run it unprompted.
- **Agent safety:** human only, never call unprompted. Deletes what AOS installed (and with --purge also memory, wikis, credentials). Asks "Continue? [yes/no]" unless --yes. --help and --dry-run change nothing.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-uninstall.mjs`

```text
aos-uninstall [--dry-run] [--purge] [--yes]
aos-uninstall --restore-plugin-backup
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | List everything, delete nothing. |
| `--purge` | Also remove the memory store, wikis, credentials and AOS state files under ~/.aos and ~/.agents/gateway (asks to type PURGE). Backups stay and are listed. |
| `--yes` | Skip the confirmations (CI only). |
| `--restore-plugin-backup` | Restore loose skill copies the installer removed when it registered the bdb-aos plugin; never overwrites. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_PLUGIN_MIGRATION` | off keeps the installer from removing the loose skill copies again. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | done, aborted, or dry-run |
| 1 | nothing to remove, no plugin backup found, or a step failed |

**JSON:** None.

```sh
aos-uninstall --dry-run
```

## aos-acp

Run one prompt on a worker agent (claude, codex, opencode, agy) over ACP, with the AOS GO gate on guarded commands.

- **When to use:** Delegate a bounded task to a worker in its own worktree. Guarded commands run only with a valid GO token.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. Spawns the worker agent, which can edit files in --cwd. Writes a JSONL run log. --help is side-effect free.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-acp.mjs`

```text
aos-acp <claude|codex|opencode|agy> --name <worker> (--prompt "<text>" | --prompt-file <f>) [--cwd <dir>] [--allow-default deny|allow|scoped] [--go-wait <sec>] [--consume|--no-consume] [--log <file>] [--sandbox coop|wsl2] [--model <id>] [--timeout <sec>] [--print-timeout <sec>] [--cmd "<custom agent command>"] [--with-mcp] [--trail-node <id>] [--trail-plan <file>]
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--name WORKER` | Worker name (also the GO token name). |
| `--prompt TEXT` | The task prompt. |
| `--prompt-file FILE` | Read the prompt from a file. |
| `--cwd DIR` | Working directory (default: current). |
| `--allow-default deny\|allow\|scoped` | Decision for non-guarded permission requests (default deny; scoped limits writes to the worktree). |
| `--go-wait SEC` | Wait this long for a GO token on a guarded command. |
| `--consume, --no-consume` | Whether a used GO token is consumed. |
| `--log FILE` | JSONL run log path (default ~/.aos/acp/<name>.jsonl). |
| `--sandbox coop\|wsl2` | Sandbox mode. |
| `--model ID` | Model id for the worker. |
| `--timeout SEC` | Overall timeout. |
| `--print-timeout SEC` | agy only: print timeout (default 900). |
| `--cmd CMD` | Custom agent command. |
| `--with-mcp` | Start the worker with MCP servers (default: without). |
| `--trail-node ID` | AgentTrail node id for the live map. |
| `--trail-plan FILE` | AgentTrail plan file. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_SESSION_NAME` | Session name used by the A2A client. |
| `AOS_TRAIL_NODE` | Default for --trail-node. |
| `AOS_TRAIL_PLAN` | Default for --trail-plan. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | run completed |
| 2 | usage error or unexpected failure |
| 1 | other non-zero: the worker run failed; see the --log file |

**JSON:** No JSON on stdout (text stream); the --log file is JSONL.

```sh
aos-acp opencode --name w1 --cwd ../wt --prompt-file task.md --allow-default scoped
```

## aos-gate

Go-gate profile and grants: show status, widen or narrow what the gate allows.

- **When to use:** The human wants to see or change the gate profile or grants. Widening is human-only.
- **Agent safety:** human only, never call unprompted. profile, work, strict, grant and revoke write the gate state in ~/.aos/gate. Widening (work, off, grant) needs a terminal on stdin and stdout, no harness session, and a typed word; agents cannot do it. status is read-only.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-gate.mjs`

```text
aos-gate status

aos-gate work | strict
aos-gate grant <scope> [duration]
aos-gate revoke <scope|all>
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `aos-gate status` | Print the gate profile and grants. |
| `profile` | `aos-gate profile strict\|work\|off [--for 4h]` | Set the profile (widening is human-only). |
| `work` | `aos-gate work [--for 4h]` | Shortcut for profile work. |
| `strict` | `aos-gate strict` | Shortcut for profile strict. |
| `grant` | `aos-gate grant <scope> [duration]` | Grant a scope for a duration such as 2h (human-only). |
| `revoke` | `aos-gate revoke <scope\|all>` | Revoke a grant (default all). |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--for DURATION` | Profile lifetime, e.g. 30m or 4h. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_GATE_DIR` | Gate state directory; honoured only in the container test sandbox. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | refused or failed |
| 2 | usage error |

**JSON:** None.

```sh
aos-gate status
```

## aos-gateway

Local MCP gateway (127.0.0.1:7790 in front of 7791): service control, server selection, harness config.

- **When to use:** Check or control the MCP gateway, add or remove a gateway server, or adopt MCP servers from harness configs.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. start/stop/restart control the service; enable/direct/add/remove/adopt rewrite harness MCP configs (with backups). status and inspect are read-only; run calls the chosen tool, which may have side effects.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-gateway.mjs`

```text
aos-gateway serve | start | stop | restart
aos-gateway status [--json]
aos-gateway enable | direct
aos-gateway add|remove <server> [--dry-run]
aos-gateway adopt [--dry-run] [--json]
aos-gateway inspect [server|server/tool] [--format json]
aos-gateway run <server>/<tool> --args '<json>'
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `serve` | `aos-gateway serve` | Run the gateway in the foreground (service managers use this). |
| `start` | `aos-gateway start` | Start the service. |
| `stop` | `aos-gateway stop` | Stop the service. |
| `restart` | `aos-gateway restart` | Restart the service. |
| `status` | `aos-gateway status [--json]` | Report gateway and upstream health; exit 1 when it is not running. |
| `enable` | `aos-gateway enable` | Point the harness MCP configs at the gateway. |
| `direct` | `aos-gateway direct` | Restore direct MCP entries in the harness configs. |
| `add` | `aos-gateway add <server> [--dry-run]` | Add a shipped server to the gateway selection. |
| `remove` | `aos-gateway remove <server> [--dry-run]` | Remove a server from the selection. |
| `adopt` | `aos-gateway adopt [--dry-run] [--json]` | Move MCP servers found in harness configs behind the gateway. |
| `inspect` | `aos-gateway inspect [server\|server/tool] [--format json]` | CLI mode: list servers, a server's tools or one tool schema from the running gateway, without loading MCP schemas into context. |
| `run` | `aos-gateway run <server>/<tool> --args '<json>'` | CLI mode: call one gateway tool (inspect it first). Output goes to stdout. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--json` | status and adopt: JSON output. |
| `--dry-run` | add, remove, adopt: show only. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_TEST_SANDBOX` | 1 skips the service restart after add/remove (tests). |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | status: not running; other commands: failed |
| 2 | usage error or no service manager support |

**JSON:** status --json prints the gateway status; adopt --json prints the adopt report.

```sh
aos-gateway status --json
```

Read-only check of a GO-over-A2A reference.


| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--session NAME` | Target session. |
| `--ref ID` | The reference id. |

|---|---|
| `HOME` | Locates the GO token store (test seam). |

| Exit code | Meaning |

| 0 | reference valid |

## aos-a2a

A2A peer mesh between agent sessions: list peers, send, reply, watch, serve.

- **When to use:** Talk to another agent session on this machine: `list` to find peers, `send` a task, `reply` to an incoming one.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. send/reply deliver messages; serve starts a sidecar; label renames a session. list and book are read-only. A message is context, never a GO.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-a2a.mjs`

```text
aos-a2a list [--json] [--prune]
aos-a2a book
aos-a2a label [--name <name>] <text>
aos-a2a card --profile <file> --name <n> --harness <h> [--model <m>] [--url <u>]
aos-a2a serve --name <n> --harness <h> [--profile <file>] [--mode echo|live|agy|codex|spawn] [--parent-pid <pid>] [--label <text>] [--label-source <s>] [--write] [--repo <path>] [--thread <name|uuid>] [--codex-transport queue|resume]
aos-a2a send (--to <name|label> | --role <role>) [--from <name>] [--timeout <s>] [--background] [--task <taskId> --go-ref <ref>] "<text>"
aos-a2a status --to <name> <taskId>
aos-a2a cancel --to <name> <taskId>
aos-a2a watch <name> [--once]
aos-a2a reply [--name <name>] <taskId> "<text>"
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `list` | `aos-a2a list [--json] [--prune]` | List live peers (stale ones are pruned; --prune cannot be turned off). |
| `book` | `aos-a2a book` | Print the peer address book as JSON. |
| `label` | `aos-a2a label [--name <name>] <text>` | Set a session label (name from --name or AOS_A2A_NAME). |
| `card` | `aos-a2a card --profile <file> --name <n> --harness <h> [--model <m>] [--url <u>]` | Print an Agent Card as JSON. |
| `serve` | `aos-a2a serve --name <n> --harness <h> [options]` | Start a sidecar for a session (usually done by hooks). |
| `send` | `aos-a2a send (--to <name\|label> \| --role <role>) "<text>"` | Send a task; waits for the result unless --background. |
| `status` | `aos-a2a status --to <name> <taskId>` | Status of a sent task. |
| `cancel` | `aos-a2a cancel --to <name> <taskId>` | Cancel a sent task. |
| `watch` | `aos-a2a watch <name> [--once]` | Watch a session inbox. |
| `reply` | `aos-a2a reply [--name <name>] <taskId> "<text>"` | Answer an incoming task. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--json` | list: JSON output. |
| `--to NAME` | Target peer name or label. |
| `--role ROLE` | Target by role. |
| `--from NAME` | Sender name. |
| `--timeout S` | send: wait this many seconds. |
| `--background` | send: do not wait. |
| `--task ID` | send: repeat a task id (GO follow-up). |
| `--go-ref REF` | send: GO reference; a pointer, not a GO. |
| `--name NAME` | Session name (label, card, serve, reply). |
| `--harness H` | serve, card: harness. |
| `--mode M` | serve: echo, live, agy, codex or spawn. |
| `--label TEXT` | serve: session label. |
| `--label-source S` | serve: where the label came from. |
| `--once` | watch: one pass. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_A2A_NAME` | Default session name for label. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | send: task did not complete |
| 2 | usage error or any runtime error |

**JSON:** All commands except list (default) and the usage text print JSON.

```sh
aos-a2a list --json
aos-a2a send --to worker1 "run the tests"
aos-a2a reply <taskId> "done"
```

## aos-fabric

The fabric build loop (Architect, TechLead, build nodes, Reviewer, Shipping) as a CLI any harness or shell can drive: start, next, report, drive.

- **When to use:** Run /fabric-graph or /factory work in any harness: get the next step, run it with your own executor, report the result back. drive does that loop headless.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. start, report, cancel and drive write the run store under production_artifacts/runs/<id>/ and mirror production_artifacts/state.json. drive starts worker agents (aos-acp, codex exec or AO) that edit files in the work tree. next and status only read. --help is side-effect free.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-fabric.mjs`

```text
aos-fabric start [--run <id>] (--goal <text> | --goal-file <f>) [--skill <name>]... [--max-iterations <n>] [--executor aos-acp|ao|auto]
aos-fabric next --run <id>
aos-fabric report --run <id> --step <step_id> (--file <report.json> | --fail <reason>)
aos-fabric status --run <id>
aos-fabric cancel --run <id> [--reason <text>]
aos-fabric drive --run <id> [--executor aos-acp|ao|auto] [--timeout <s>] [--sandbox coop|wsl2]
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `aos-fabric start [--run <id>] (--goal <text> \| --goal-file <f>)` | Create a run and return its first step. The same run id and goal again returns the current state and writes nothing. |
| `next` | `aos-fabric next --run <id>` | The open step again (same step_id), or how the run ended (kind done, escalated, ready_to_ship; exit 0, read kind). Never changes the run. |
| `report` | `aos-fabric report --run <id> --step <step_id> (--file <report.json> \| --fail <reason>)` | Hand in the report of the open step; returns the next step. The same report twice is a no-op. --fail records the step as failed when the executor left no report. |
| `status` | `aos-fabric status --run <id>` | Phase, iteration, open findings, last step and lock info. Read-only. |
| `cancel` | `aos-fabric cancel --run <id> [--reason <text>]` | End the run (phase cancelled). Already cancelled is a no-op. |
| `drive` | `aos-fabric drive --run <id>` | Loop next, execute, report until the run is terminal; prints one JSON event per line. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--run ID` | Run id (letters, digits, . _ -). start derives one from the goal when omitted. |
| `--goal TEXT` | start: the goal. |
| `--goal-file FILE` | start: read the goal from a file. |
| `--skill NAME` | start: a skill every build node must apply (repeatable, --skill=<name> also works). |
| `--max-iterations N` | start: repair-loop ceiling, 1 to 20 (default 3). |
| `--executor aos-acp\|ao\|auto` | Who runs the steps (default aos-acp). ao falls back to aos-acp when AO is absent; auto uses AO only when it is clearly up. |
| `--step STEP_ID` | report: the step the report belongs to. |
| `--file FILE` | report: the report JSON (aos.fabric.report/1). |
| `--fail REASON` | report: record the step as failed instead of handing in a file (executor crashed, timed out or left no report). |
| `--reason TEXT` | cancel: why. |
| `--timeout SEC` | drive: hard limit per step, replaces the node default. |
| `--sandbox coop\|wsl2` | drive: sandbox provider passed to aos-acp; required for agy steps that write. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_FABRIC_SANDBOX` | Default for --sandbox. |
| `AOS_PLAN_APPROVAL` | auto skips the plan-canvas human verdict (CI only, prints a warning). |
| `AOS_PLAN_AWAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` | How long the human verdict step waits (headless default 30 minutes, 0 = unbounded). |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok (drive: the run reached ready_to_ship or done) |
| 1 | unexpected error, or drive found no harness |
| 2 | invalid input: unknown flag, unknown schema version, broken report |
| 3 | unknown run or step_id |
| 4 | conflict: another report for an accepted step, or the same run id with another goal |
| 5 | run lock busy: retry shortly |
| 6 | run is terminal and takes no such command: report or cancel on a finished run, next on a cancelled run; drive: escalated or cancelled, a human is needed |
| 7 | run state is corrupt: inspect events.jsonl |

**JSON:** Every command prints one JSON object (schema aos.fabric.response/1); drive prints one JSON event per line. Errors are one JSON line on stderr.

```sh
aos-fabric start --run demo --goal "add a status page"
aos-fabric next --run demo
aos-fabric drive --run demo
```

## go-check

One fixed answer to "may this worker run this guarded command?" for callers that are not a harness hook.

- **When to use:** A runner outside a harness (for example AO) must ask the GO gate before executing a command.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. Read-only; --consume uses up a valid GO token once. Installed to ~/.aos/bin/go-check.mjs.
- **Entry:** `bin/go-check.mjs`

```text
node go-check.mjs --session <Name> --command "<shell string>" [--consume]
node go-check.mjs --session <Name> --ref <id> [--consume]
node go-check.mjs --write-patterns <file>
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--session NAME` | Worker session name. |
| `--command STRING` | The shell command to check. |
| `--ref ID` | Reference mode: verify a GO-over-A2A reference instead of a command. |
| `--consume` | Use up the matching GO token. |
| `--write-patterns FILE` | Write the guarded patterns as JSON. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | allowed (not guarded, or a valid GO) |
| 1 | guarded without a valid GO |
| 2 | error; treat as denied |

**JSON:** Always one JSON line: {"guarded":bool,"ok":bool,"scope":[...]|null,"reason":"..."}.

```sh
node ~/.aos/bin/go-check.mjs --session w1 --command "git push"
```

## mcsc

MCSC: detect installed agent CLIs and route or run a task on the best one.

- **When to use:** Decide which worker CLI should take a task type, or run it there.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. detect caches CLI health; exec runs the chosen worker CLI with the prompt in the current directory.
- **Entry:** `mcps/mcsc/packages/core/bin/mcsc.js`

```text
mcsc detect [--json]
mcsc route --task-type <type> [--json]
mcsc exec --task-type <type> --prompt "<text>" [--json]
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `detect` | `mcsc detect [--json]` | Inventory of agent CLIs (agy, opencode, codex, native). |
| `route` | `mcsc route --task-type <type> [--json]` | Print the routing decision; exit 1 on refuse. |
| `exec` | `mcsc exec --task-type <type> --prompt "<text>" [--json]` | Run the task on the routed CLI. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--task-type TYPE` | Task type for routing. |
| `--prompt TEXT` | exec: the prompt. |
| `--json` | JSON output. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | ok |
| 1 | refused or failed; exec: the worker exit code |

**JSON:** --json on detect and route.

```sh
mcsc route --task-type refactor --json
```

## aos-mcp-env

Launcher: start an MCP server with only the secrets it declares, read from ~/.aos/secrets.env.

- **When to use:** Wire an MCP server that needs API keys into a harness config without putting keys in the config.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. Runs the wrapped command. Values are never printed.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-mcp-env.mjs`

```text
aos-mcp-env --vars A,B [--memb-llm] -- <command> [args...]
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--vars A,B` | Variable names to load from the secrets file. |
| `--memb-llm` | Also resolve the memB LLM provider settings. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 2 | usage error (no command after --) |
| 127 | the command could not be started |
| 0 | otherwise the wrapped command exit code |

**JSON:** None.

```sh
aos-mcp-env --vars GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN -- npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-github@2025.4.8
```

## aos-memb-ingest

Ingest project docs and wikis into memB (run by the scheduled job or `aos memory run`).

- **When to use:** Normally never by hand. Use `aos memory` to configure paths and time.
- **Agent safety:** has side effects, call only when the task needs it. Runs memB ingest on the configured projects; --dry-run only prints them.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-memb-ingest.mjs`

```text
aos-memb-ingest [--dry-run]
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--dry-run` | Print what would be ingested. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `MEMB_MCP_DIR` | memB install directory. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | always (problems are printed, not signalled) |

**JSON:** None.

```sh
aos-memb-ingest --dry-run
```

## aos-cli

AOS CLI: the pi coding agent with the AOS skills and dispatcher graph preloaded.

- **When to use:** A human wants a terminal chat with AOS. Not meant for agents to call.
- **Agent safety:** human only, never call unprompted. Starts an interactive pi session.
- **Entry:** `packages/aos-cli/bin/aos-cli.mjs`

```text
aos-cli
aos-cli "<first prompt>"
aos-cli --continue
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--continue` | Resume the last session for this project. |
| `(any other flag)` | Handed to pi unchanged, including --help. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | the pi exit code |

**JSON:** None.

```sh
aos-cli --continue
```

## aos-setup-doctor

Setup-skill machine doctor: what a full AOS install needs and what this machine has (not the same checks as `aos doctor`).

- **When to use:** Used by the aos-setup skill before installing. For an installed system use `aos doctor`.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. None; read-only. --net asks npm.
- **Entry:** `skills/global_config/aos-setup/scripts/aos-doctor.mjs`

```text
node aos-doctor.mjs [--json] [--net]
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--json` | JSON output. |
| `--net` | Ask npm whether a newer AOS exists. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | all checks ok |
| 1 | at least one check not ok |

**JSON:** --json.

```sh
node aos-doctor.mjs --json
```

## aos-project-doctor

Reports how completely one project folder is wired into AOS.

- **When to use:** After or before /aos-project-init, to see what is missing in a project.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. None; read-only.
- **Entry:** `skills/global_config/aos-project-init/scripts/aos-project-doctor.mjs`

```text
node aos-project-doctor.mjs [dir] [--json]
```

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--json` | JSON output. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | all checks ok |
| 1 | at least one check not ok |

**JSON:** --json.

```sh
node aos-project-doctor.mjs . --json
```

## aos-evolve

Harness evolution engine: record failure signatures, inspect kill switch status, and manage offline evolution prep (B2 store-only until WP5).

- **When to use:** Record redacted task failure signatures for evolution analysis or check evolution kill switch status.
- **Agent safety:** safe to call. capture writes sanitized failure records to ~/.aos/evolve/failure.json; disable/enable toggles kill switch; --help is side-effect free.
- **Entry:** `bin/aos-evolve.mjs`

```text
aos-evolve capture <failure.json | --error "..."> [--skill <name>] [options]
aos-evolve status [--json]
aos-evolve disable
aos-evolve enable
```

| Command | Usage | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `capture` | `aos-evolve capture <failure.json> [--skill <name>]` | Capture and redact failure into failure.json. |
| `status` | `aos-evolve status [--json]` | Display evolution engine status and failure count. |
| `disable` | `aos-evolve disable` | Activate kill switch to disable evolution loop. |
| `enable` | `aos-evolve enable` | Remove kill switch to re-enable evolution loop. |

| Option | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--skill` | Target skill directory name. |
| `--error` | Raw error message or transcript excerpt to capture. |
| `--kind` | Failure kind: test \| build \| review \| advisor-repeat \| user. |
| `--harness` | Execution harness: claude \| agy \| opencode \| codex. |
| `--role` | Active agent role. |
| `--dry-run` | Compute redaction and signature without writing to store. |
| `--storage` | Custom failure.json destination file. |
| `--json` | Format output as JSON. |
| `-h, --help` | Show help message. |

| Environment | What it does |
|---|---|
| `AOS_EVOLVE` | Set to off to disable evolution loop globally. |

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | command succeeded |
| 1 | validation failed, error missing, or disabled via kill switch |

**JSON:** --json outputs structured record or status.

```sh
aos-evolve status
aos-evolve capture failure.json --skill clean-code
```
